issues.t: Sudden unintended acceleration or stuck throttle
issues.sym: The van speeds up on its own, keeps accelerating after you lift off the pedal, or the engine races even in Park. Owners describe brakes struggling to hold it.
issues.why: Several owners of 1996 and 1997 Previas reported this to NHTSA, but no single defect was confirmed and there was no recall for it. A sticking throttle, a fault in the idle or cruise control, or something jamming the pedal are the usual things to rule out.
issues.next: If it happens, brake firmly with both feet, shift to Neutral and pull over, then switch the engine off. Do not drive the van again until a shop has inspected the throttle, cruise control and pedal area.

issues.t: Overheating, coolant loss and blown head gasket
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, especially on long hills, you lose coolant, see steam or white smoke, or the engine loses power.
issues.why: The Previa engine sits under the floor with long coolant hoses running front to back, so leaks can go unnoticed. Once it overheats, the head gasket can fail. Owners have reported overheating, coolant spraying over the engine and head gasket failure.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off as soon as the gauge climbs. Don't keep driving an overheating engine. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the engine checked for a head gasket leak before more damage is done.

issues.t: Front differential can leak oil at high speed (recall)
issues.sym: Oil around the front differential on All-Trac (AWD) vans, and eventually a whine or grinding from the front of the van. Most owners notice nothing until the recall is done.
issues.why: On some 1997 All-Trac Previas, a gap inside the front differential let oil escape through the air breather when the van was driven for long periods above 75 mph. Low oil can wreck the differential bearings and lock the unit up.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check your VIN for recall 97V056. The fix is a modified breather plug, done free. Also have the front differential oil level checked.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks or brakes feel weak
issues.sym: The pedal goes down further than normal, the van takes longer to stop, or the brakes seem to stop working.
issues.why: Owners reported brake master cylinder and brake booster failures on 1996 Previas. Toyota also released a newer-style master cylinder with a built-in proportioning valve for these vans.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Treat a soft or sinking pedal as urgent and do not drive the van until a brake shop checks it. Ask them to inspect the master cylinder, booster and lines for leaks.

issues.t: Vibration through the pedal when braking
issues.sym: A shaking or pulsing brake pedal and steering wheel when you slow down, mostly from highway speed.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletins for front brake vibration on these Previas and changed the front pad material to reduce it. Warped or worn front rotors cause the same feel.
issues.next: Have the front pads and rotors measured. New rotors (or resurfaced ones, if thick enough) with the updated pads usually cure it.

issues.t: ABS light on or antilock brakes not working
issues.sym: The ABS warning light stays on, or the antilock system does not seem to work in a hard stop.
issues.why: Owners filed complaints about the antilock brakes failing on 1996 Previas. A bad wheel speed sensor, wiring or the ABS control unit can switch the system off.
issues.next: Normal brakes should still work, but drive gently and leave more room. Have the ABS trouble codes read so the right part is replaced.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifting poorly at high mileage
issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, no shift into 4th (overdrive), slipping, or a jolt when you select Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: RepairPal lists incorrect shifting as a common Previa problem from roughly 125,000 to 150,000 miles. Owners also report failed shift solenoids and overdrive problems.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition first. If shifting stays wrong, have the codes read and the shift solenoids tested before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Failed emissions test from clogged EGR passages
issues.sym: Check engine light, failing a smog or emissions test, and sometimes pinging under load.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) system over time and blocks the flow, usually somewhere around 100,000 to 125,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the EGR valve and passages inspected. Cleaning the carbon out is often enough; a stuck valve gets replaced.

issues.t: Worn front struts: clunking and bottoming out
issues.sym: Clunks from the front over small bumps, then the front bottoming out over potholes, with a bouncy ride.
issues.why: The front struts and their mounts wear out with mileage. One owner noted the job is unusually involved on the Previa because part of the dash has to come out.
issues.next: Have the front struts and mounts inspected. Replace them as a pair and get an alignment afterwards.

issues.t: Supercharger oil never checked or changed
issues.sym: Usually no sign until the supercharger is low on oil; then a whine or rattle from the supercharger and less power.
issues.why: The supercharger has its own small oil supply, checked at a fill screw from under the van rather than with a dipstick. One owner noted the owner's manual doesn't mention checking it, so it is often forgotten.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check the supercharger oil level and condition at the next service. Catching it low can save the supercharger.

issues.sym: The front A/C works but the rear vents blow warm or weak air.
issues.why: Toyota released an improved rear A/C magnetic valve because corrosion inside the original valve could stop it working.
issues.next: Have an A/C shop check the rear magnetic valve and refrigerant charge before replacing larger parts.

issues.t: Musty smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A damp, musty or sour smell when the A/C is first turned on.
issues.why: Moisture and mold build up on the A/C evaporator. Toyota issued a bulletin covering evaporator odor on several models, including these Previas.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air intake filter if fitted and have the evaporator cleaned and treated. Make sure the A/C drain isn't blocked.

issues.t: Clunk or vibration from the drive shaft coupling
issues.sym: A clunk when pulling away or shifting into gear, or a vibration under the van that changes with speed.
issues.why: The Previa's drive shaft has a flexible coupling joint. Toyota released a coupling kit for it in 2000, and a worn coupling lets the shaft knock and shake.
issues.next: Have the drive shaft coupling, U-joints and center bearing inspected on a lift.

issues.t: Sliding door or door locks not working
issues.sym: The sliding door sticks, won't latch or open properly, the door locks stop working, or a sliding door window fails.
issues.why: Owners filed complaints about the sliding door, door locks and sliding-door window on these vans. Worn rollers, latches and lock parts are typical causes on an older van.
issues.next: Make sure the sliding door fully latches before driving, especially with children aboard. Have the latch, rollers and lock mechanism repaired.

issues.sym: The wipers stop, park in the wrong place, or only work on some speeds.
issues.why: Owners reported wiper failures on 1996 Previas. A worn wiper motor, linkage or switch is the usual cause.
issues.next: Don't drive in rain or snow without working wipers. Have the wiper motor, linkage and switch tested.

issues.sym: One or both headlights flicker or switch off for a moment while driving.
issues.why: An owner reported both headlights cutting out on a 1996 Previa. Worn headlight switch contacts, connectors or relays are common causes on a van this age.
issues.next: Avoid night driving until it's fixed. Ask a shop to check the headlight switch, relay and connectors for heat damage.

issues.t: Catalytic converter or exhaust pipe failure
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, a rattle under the van, a rotten-egg smell or a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners reported catalytic converter and exhaust pipe failures on 1997 Previas. Age, rust and engine misfires wear these parts out.
issues.next: Exhaust leaks can let fumes into the cabin, so get it checked soon. Fix any misfire first so a new converter isn't damaged.

issues.sym: Coolant drips or a crusty residue near the front of the engine, a sweet smell, and a falling coolant level.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out with age. RepairPal and YourMechanic both show water pump replacement as a regular Previa repair.
issues.next: Top up with the right coolant and watch the temperature gauge. Replace the pump soon, before a leak causes overheating.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leak from the pressure hose
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid under the van, a whine when turning, or steering that feels heavier.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose gets old and starts seeping. Both RepairPal and YourMechanic list it as a Previa repair, and it is a big job because of how the hose is routed.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and top it up. Have the leak traced, since running the pump low can damage it.
